svg.aria-label: Diagram: the three ways to run an agent in Amazon Bedrock as of the Bedrock Managed Agents preview, and how they relate. On the left, Amazon Bedrock Agents, now renamed Amazon Bedrock Agents Classic, which is no longer open to new customers; existing customers can continue to use the service as normal, and AWS publishes a maintenance mode page for it. Its original proposition was that you do not have to provision capacity, manage infrastructure or write custom code, because Bedrock manages prompt engineering, memory, monitoring, encryption, user permissions and API invocation. In the centre, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, which AWS recommends instead: an agentic platform for building, deploying and operating agents at scale using any framework and any foundation model, working with open-source frameworks including CrewAI, LangGraph, LlamaIndex and Strands Agents. It comprises thirteen modular services usable together or independently, namely Harness, Runtime, Memory, Gateway, Identity, Code Interpreter, Browser, Observability, Payments, Evaluations, Optimization, Policy and Registry. Two of these matter for the comparison. AgentCore Harness is a managed agent loop invoked with a single API call where you specify a model, system prompt and tools inline, with Harness handling orchestration, tool execution, memory management and response generation, each session running in an isolated microVM with filesystem and shell access, and it works with Amazon Bedrock, OpenAI, Google Gemini and any OpenAI-compatible provider. AgentCore Runtime is a serverless runtime with true session isolation that already supports the OpenAI Agents SDK among other frameworks, plus protocols including MCP and A2A. On the right, the new Bedrock Managed Agents preview, built on a customized version of OpenAI's Agents API engineered to be AWS-native, which manages state, tool selection and use, code execution and multi-step coordination, available in preview in only three Regions being North Virginia, Oregon and Ohio, at no additional charge beyond underlying resources during preview with pricing subject to change at general availability. A closing panel records the overlap question: AgentCore Harness is already a managed agent loop that already works with OpenAI, and AgentCore Runtime already supports the OpenAI Agents SDK, so the new preview duplicates capability that is already generally available, and the documentation does not say when to choose which.
svg.title: Three agent runtimes, the first one closed, the newest overlapping the middle
svg.text: The announcement is the third runtime. The news is that the first one is closed.
That fact is in the documentation, not in any release note, and it is the actionable one.
thirteen modular services, used together or alone:
Policy intercepts every tool call before execution
The overlap the announcement does not mention
AgentCore Harness is already “a managed agent loop… with a single API call” — and already works with Amazon
Bedrock, OpenAI, Google Gemini and any OpenAI-compatible provider. Sessions run in an isolated microVM
with filesystem and shell access. AgentCore Runtime already supports the OpenAI Agents SDK.
So the difference is whose loop semantics you get — AWS’s or OpenAI’s — and nothing published says when to pick which.
Starting today → AgentCore. Documented, GA, recommended, and it already reaches OpenAI models and SDK.
Porting an existing OpenAI Agents app, in a US Region, non-sensitive data → BMA is plausibly the shortest path.
On Bedrock Agents today → you are on Classic. Read the maintenance mode page; the migration target is AgentCore.
Write tools as MCP servers: Gateway converts APIs and Lambda into MCP tools, Runtime speaks MCP and A2A, and BMA connects
tools via MCP servers. It is the one asset that survives a change of runtime.
AgentCore “may use and store your content to improve your service experience” — for your use, not other customers’.
Treat a preview’s pricing as unknown rather than zero. The announcement says so itself.
